round_5.note: This box carried about eight other agents throughout (load average 30-41), and a 4-second binary's own CPU time varied 4.0-6.4 s with it, so an arm's minimum is its luckiest run and the interleaved min-of-15 is not reliable at the +-5% scale (kmod measured +9.4% by min and +1.7% by the median of the per-pair ratio in the SAME run). The primary number is therefore the redo pass's share of the run's own first pass, measured inside one process, which is what the option costs: nothing else about the run changes.

round_4.char_pointer_pointer: a char ** vote is refused where a pointer-width value loaded through the input or stored through it has a constant wider than a byte stored through it (splits_a_wide_constant, one level down); a pointer-to-pointer passed as the address of a caller's frame object is marked (Typed.frame) and refused where the callee loads or stores through it anywhere but [0, pointer width) (reaches_past_the_pointee); any vote is refused for a value used as the index of a PTRADD (indexes_a_pointer). Refusing every frame address instead costs 17 functions (parse_line(&keyword,&arg), next_field(&line), simple_strtoul(&p), quote_name_buf(&inbuf)): measured, not shipped
round_4.lone_field: a lone field no longer replaces a pointee a declared prototype the parameter is handed to gave it (pipe (int *)); a taken caller vote is kept for a record, and for a char ** when the field is a whole aligned pointer; a char * vote, or a char ** read as an int at offset 4 (expr getsize), yields to the record. The reviewer's literal rule (keep every committed pointee, only void * / undefined accept) was measured: -137 functions credited (find O0 insert_primary etc.: an int * protoorder carried from a callee reading the enum at offset 0), 2,128 -> 2,120 credited perfect; the shipped rule is identical to round 3 on the typesweep

round_5.committed_claim: (a) taken: the code always required a record to carry its layout, so the catalog, spec 04, cli.md, the module doc and the PR body no longer claim a libc shell or FILE *; a FILE * is voted only under --option libctypes glibc. The unit test asserts an incomplete FILE shell is NOT committed and a laid-out record of the same name is. (b) was refused: a shell says no more than void * and the member-fit and reaches_past_the_pointee refusals have no fields to read, so letting shells vote would loosen the option rather than fix a claim.
round_5.redo_bound: CALLEE_VOTE_MAX_LINES = 32 printed lines of the FIRST decompile; the function is dropped from the ledger before decide(), so nothing is stated, no round pays, and seed/converge have nothing to apply. Chosen from the measured redo profile (per-redo length, ms and whether the body changed) and validated by the redo share: 32 lines keeps kmod at 3.4-4.3% (40 lines 5.7-7.6%, unbounded 13.6-14.5%).
round_5.why_not_an_oracle: Skipping only the redos that change nothing would leave kmod at about +8.5% and crontab at +9.0%: 20 of kmod's 58 redos are wasted but they are 147 of its 571 ms, and crontab's whole cost is one 189-line redo that does change its body.
